summary: Klamath County, OR steel tower built 1932 on Swan Lake Point; gone by 1976 or dismantled 1979; the summit is now a Forest Service communications site.

facts.design: 80-foot steel tower with cabin, plus a separate ground cabin for living quarters completed in 1934
facts.status_note: Tower and cabin reported gone by 1976 (FFLOS and firelookout.com) or dismantled in 1979 (Oregon Forest Lookouts); no source describes what remains

staffing.status: manned only during periods of peak fire danger

access.note: Summit is a Forest Service communications site under special-use authorizations (2011 and 2014 decisions); no source says the public may visit

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service; built for the Klamath Indian Agency

events.note: Eighty-foot steel tower bought for the proposed lookout; tower and freight expected to cost about $1,140
Tower and cabin erected; the register dates the build to 1932
Ground cabin for living quarters completed December 27 at a cost of $839.60
Claude Parazoo and his wife, with their family, stationed at the lookout for the summer; by early September Mrs. Parazoo was moving to the Klamath Agency lookout for the rest of the season
Brush fire near Lone Pine spotted by the lookout guard; about eight-tenths of an acre; put out by a six-man crew
Forest memo says the station needs replacing and that a new one may take several years
Lookout manned only during periods of peak fire danger
Tower and cabin reported gone by 1976 (FFLOS and firelookout.com)
Oregon Forest Lookouts says the lookout was dismantled
Registered June 12, 2011 as FFLOS US 1048, OR 406
Forest Service decision signed September 23, 2011, to upgrade facilities at the communications site
Forest Service decision signed June 7, 2014, for a BPA radio station upgrade, including removal of existing structures

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS and firelookout.com say the tower was gone by 1976; the Oregon Forest Lookouts page says it was dismantled in 1979. The record keeps both, and the story reports both.
Most sources give 80 feet (24.4 m). An NGS data sheet quoted on the Oregon Forest Lookouts page gives 90 feet. The record keeps 24.4 m.

notes_for_editor: Coordinates conflict. Our record (42.42223, -121.69481) matches the firelookout.org Oregon list; the FFLOS detail page gives N 42.410145, W 121.663351. Not resolved here; please check before relying on the map pin. Removal date (1976 vs 1979) and height (80 vs 90 ft) are both reported in the story. No staffing or fire evidence after 1973 was found. Access level 'restricted' is inferred from the Forest Service special-use communications site; no source addresses public visits.
